structured_output.analysis: The only measured grid is iso_3.15. Its whole-recipe KL is 0.436 (E514ab09c524e), above the predicted 0.398, so layers interact. Loss is concentrated in MLP layers quantized to 2 or 3 bits. The evidence only names the methods of the high-loss layers, so I can't find low-cost downgrades to pay for upgrades. For that reason this round only changes GPTQ options and leaves every layer's method alone. Turning on act_order and changing damp do not change the stored bits, so these grids stay within the budget.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Most of the loss sits in GPTQ layers at 2 and 3 bits, for example 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) and 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded). The whole recipe measured 0.436 (E514ab09c524e). Turning on act_order (act_order=true) should lower GPTQ error without adding bits.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: The measured KL of 0.436 (E514ab09c524e) is above the predicted 0.398, which suggests the calibration overfits. The activation kurtosis in 27.up_proj is 1090 (E24beed188b6a). A stronger damp=0.05 together with act_order=true should make the Hessian more robust at the same bit count.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp003
proposals.rationale: This tests the damp direction opposite to the damp=0.05 grid, using damp=0.003 with act_order=true. It targets the same GPTQ low-bit losses, for example 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5). The bit count does not change.

c3.reason: The proposal's unmeasured effect is worded as an expectation: "Turning on act_order ... should lower GPTQ error without adding bits." This is borderline: the opening claim that "most of the loss sits in GPTQ layers at 2 and 3 bits" is stated as fact, and the two cited examples (0.00633 and 0.00572) don't show most of 0.436. It passes because that claim describes the current loss, not the proposal's effect.
